swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: TLV9002IDR is limited to 5.5 V max (7 V abs max, p.14) whereas TL072IDR supports up to 40 V (42 V abs max, p.10). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (TL072IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR vs TLV9002IDR: IN=RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 5.3x (TL072IDR: 5.25 MHz p.15 vs TLV9002IDR: 1 MHz p.17); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 10x (TL072IDR: 20 V/µs p.16 vs TLV9002IDR: 2 V/µs p.17); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 13x (TL072IDR: 65 pA p.15 vs TLV9002IDR: 5 pA p.17); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 23.3x (TL072IDR: 1400 µA/ch p.16 vs TLV9002IDR: 60 µA/ch p.18); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: TLV9002IDR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (7 V, p.14) than TL072IDR (42 V, p.10); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 7 V.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 41% higher on TLV9002IDR (TL072IDR: 147.8 °C/W p.11 vs TLV9002IDR: 207.9 °C/W p.15); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: TL072IDR requires Vs,min >= 4.5 V (p.11) vs 1.8 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (TL072IDR: -40..85 °C Industrial (-40°C to 85°C) vs TLV9002IDR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 125°C)); TL072IDR hot limit only 85 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: TL072IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and TLV9002IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because supply voltage Vs,max drops >=20%; rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; GBWP differs 5.3x. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 5.25 MHz (p.15) vs 1 MHz (p.17), supply ceiling 40 V (p.11) vs 5.5 V (p.14), Vos 6 mV (p.15) vs 1.6 mV (p.17), Ib 13x gap (65 vs 5 pA), voltage noise 37 vs 30 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: TL072IDR "Negative-Rail Input Headroom Limit and Legacy Phase Reversal Trap" (p.11) and TLV9002IDR "5.5 V Max Supply Limit vs Pin-Identical High-Voltage SOIC-8 Op-Amps" (p.14). BOM decision: Choose TL072IDR when supply rails exceed 5.5 V (rated up to 40 V) or closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 5.25 MHz GBWP; choose TLV9002IDR when DC precision demands <= 1.6 mV max Vos or high-impedance sensors require pA-class input bias (5 pA). Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.5 vs TOP_VIEW p.8) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
